types.str: A borrowed view of text (pointer and length). String literals are `str`. These are the methods you can call on one: `s.find("x")`.
types.String: An owned, growable string. Appending: `s += "text"`. Methods below work on `String` too (a `String` converts to `str`).

conv.description: Both functions accept an optional sign and decimal digits only. Whitespace, `1e3` and `0x10` are rejected with `InvalidDigit`.

errors.Empty: the text is empty (or only a sign)
errors.InvalidDigit: a character is not a decimal digit
errors.Overflow: the number does not fit the result type

math.description: `sqrt`, `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `atan2`, `exp`, `log`, `pow`, `floor`, `ceil` and `fabs` are the libm functions of the same name (all `f64`). The `_i32`, `_i64` and `_f64` helpers exist because plain `min`/`max` live in `std.mem` and are generic.
math.example:
import std.math;

println("{:.4}", math.sqrt(2.0));        // 1.4142
println("{}", math.gcd(48, 18));          // 6
println("{}", math.max_i32(3, 9));        // 9
println("{:.5}", math.PI);                // 3.14159

consts.PI: the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter

rand.description: `Rng` is a small, fast generator. It is not cryptographically secure. Seed it with `Rng.from_seed(n)` for repeatable sequences (tests, games with replays) or `Rng.new()` to seed it from the clock.

types.Rng: A pseudo-random number generator. Methods that draw numbers need a `let mut` variable.

errors.Empty: `pop` was called on an empty list

types.List: A growable array that owns its elements. Fields: `len` (the number of elements) and the buffer. Destroyed automatically at the end of its scope.

types.Stack: A last-in, first-out stack that owns its elements.

types.Queue: A first-in, first-out queue (a ring buffer) that owns its elements.

types.HashMap: A hash map from `String` keys to values of type `V`. It owns its keys and values.

types.Tree: An ordered set in a binary search tree. `T` must implement `Ord` (a method `cmp`).
types.Node: A tree node. An implementation detail; use `Tree`.

errors.Eof: input ended before anything could be read

errors.NotFound: the file or directory does not exist

errors.NotSet: the environment variable is not set

DateTime.doc: A calendar date and time (proleptic Gregorian calendar).

fields.unix: seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC this value was made from

types.Duration: A span of time with nanosecond resolution.

errors.AcceptFailed: `accept` failed (the server socket was closed or the system ran out of descriptors)

types.Socket: A TCP socket. Closes itself at the end of its scope.

errors.SpawnFailed: the operating system could not start a thread

types.Thread: A running OS thread. Call `join` once.
types.Condvar: A condition variable, used together with a `Mutex`.
types.AtomicI64: An integer that can be read and written safely from several threads.
types.Channel: An unbounded multi-producer, multi-consumer queue. Create with `thread.channel<T>()`.

Display.doc: The trait behind `println(x)`, `to_str(x)`, `x.to_string()` and `"{x}"`. Implement it for your own types and they print the way you wrote. It is part of the prelude, so no import is needed. All built-in number types and `bool` implement it already, so `T: Display` bounds accept them.

methods.to_string: Builds the text for this value. A format such as `{p:>10}` applies to the text this returns.
